title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Spiced smoked haddock rice
excerpt: Flaked smoked haddock cooked with basmati rice, soft-boiled eggs, curry spices, and fresh parsley. An Anglo-Indian breakfast dish that also makes an excellent easy supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian breakfast dish with roots in the Indian dish khichri (rice and lentils). The British colonial version substituted smoked fish and added curry powder, and it became a fixture of Victorian and Edwardian country house breakfasts.

content.text: Kedgeree is smoked haddock flaked through spiced basmati rice with soft-boiled eggs, butter, and plenty of parsley. The haddock is poached in milk, which keeps it moist, and the poaching milk goes into the rice to cook it. The eggs are added at the end, soft enough to mix into the rice when cut.
Place the haddock in a wide pan with the milk and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 8 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Lift the fish out and set aside. Keep the poaching milk.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then peel and halve. Set aside.
Melt the butter in a large, wide pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the curry powder and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute.

Add the rice and stir to coat in the spices. Pour in 300 ml of the strained poaching milk and the vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over a low heat for 12 minutes until the rice has absorbed the liquid.

Flake the haddock, discarding the skin and any bones. Fold through the rice gently with the lemon juice and most of the parsley. Season with salt. Arrange the halved eggs on top. Scatter over the remaining parsley and serve.
